rag_pipeline.instruction: Collect PDF/PPTX/XLSX/HTML from local folder, Google Drive, bank IR, SET/SEC and BOT. Do not crawl private PC folders unless user explicitly uploads/mounts them.
Calculate SHA-256, canonical URL, document date, ticker, entity level and version. Deduplicate identical files.
Extract text plus tables; preserve page, table title, unit and footnotes. Prefer native PDF/table parsing before OCR.
Normalize units to THB mn / percent-point / bps, but retain original value and unit. Never turn missing into zero.
Chunk by semantic headings/table blocks (~800-1,500 tokens; 100-150 overlap only for narrative). Tables should remain intact where possible.
ticker, entity_level, year, quarter, document_type, page, section, source_url, published_at, audit_status, language, source_tier.
Extract financial metrics to a deterministic facts table with value, unit, period, source/page, status and confidence.
Run equation checks, unit checks, period/entity checks, QoQ/YoY consistency checks and cross-source conflict detection.
Embed narrative chunks into vector index; keep structured facts in SQL/JSON. Do NOT rely on vector RAG for numeric lookup.
For numeric questions: facts/SQL first. For explanation/thesis: vector retrieval second. Always filter ticker+period+entity level.
Return FACT / INTERPRETATION / SCENARIO separately, with page-level provenance for facts.
Flag conflicts, low confidence, stale mix, and company-vs-group mismatches before publishing.
Market/macro: daily-monthly as appropriate; C.B.1.1 monthly; financials/MD&A/presentations quarterly; Pillar 3/annual reports annually.
